_comment: Vignettes (Expansion 6 C.9, docs/ADVENTURES.md §6.11): hand-made situations, each needing particular things in the world (its vignette.needs, game/story/vignettes.py NEEDS), with its own meetings (v_...) and scenes (scenes.vignettes.json). Roles bound 'given' take what the need found; the need's words are the situation's own ({ruin}, {water}...).

note: The bell of {ruin_was} lies in the flooded crypt under {ruin}, where {water} came in the night {ruin_fall}.
Whatever lies in the drowned crypt under {ruin} has had {ruin_years} alone with the bell.
{keeper} will not go near the crypt under {ruin}: the bell lies in the black water there, and the water is deep.

label: Tell me about the night it fell.
Why was the bell taken down at all?
say: My grandmother had it from hers. They rang it to call the men in from the fields, the night {ruin_fall}. They rang it too long. It brought them straight to us. After, the ones who lived threw it in the water so it could never call anyone again.
The old ones said it rang the whole night. Rang and rang, and nobody came, and then the wrong ones came. We drowned it after, for shame. And now it rings by itself.
fail_say: It was a long time ago. All anyone ever told me was the sound. Only the sound.

label: Some things are better left under the water.
say: ...Maybe you're right. Maybe it is ringing for me, and I should just go to it.
Leave it, then. I'll stop my ears. I've had practice.

line: The bell of {ruin_was} hangs in {town} now, and once a year it is rung for the dead of {ruin}, and only once. {keeper} counts the strokes.
Raised, and hung, and rung once for every soul of {ruin_was}. Under {water}, nothing rings back.
The people of {town} stand bareheaded while the bell of {ruin_was} is rung for the dead of {ruin}. {keeper} stands at the front and does not weep.
The bell rings over {town} again. On still nights, something in the crypt under {ruin} rings back.
{keeper} wept to hear it. The fishers say the water by {ruin} has gone cold, and stays cold.
They hung the bell in {town} and rang it. Something under {ruin} answered, once, and the ringers have not gone near the water since.
The bell stays under {water}. {keeper} sits by the water at night and listens, and does not say what for.
Left where it lies. The bell of {ruin_was} still rings on still nights, and {keeper} has stopped asking anyone.
No one goes down to the crypt under {ruin}. {keeper} keeps the story of {ruin_was} alone, and listens to the water.
{keeper} was found by {water} at dawn, sitting up, eyes open, facing {ruin}. The bell had rung all night.
{keeper} went down to the water on a still night and did not come back. The bell has not rung since.
The bell rang under {water} all one night. In the morning {keeper} was gone from {town}, and the door of the house stood open.

title: The drowned bell
The bell under {water}
What rings under {water}
stakes: the bell of {ruin_was}, and the peace of {keeper}
{keeper}'s last wish, and the drowned bell
a bell under {water}, and the one who hears it ring
plea: You heard it. Don't tell me you didn't. That's the bell of {ruin_was}, {ruin_years} under the water, and it rings for us who are left. I am the last who keeps its story. Bring it up. Bring it out of the crypt at {ruin} and let it be hung where it can be seen, before it rings for me.

Every still night since the spring. The bell of {ruin}. My people were born under it, and buried under it. They threw it in the water the year {ruin_fall}, and I thought it was done with us. Raise it. Please. I want to hear it once in the light.

I hear it when the wind drops. The bell of {ruin_was}, under {water}, where our fathers sank it. I keep the story of {ruin}, and I will not be the one who lets it ring alone. Raise it from the crypt, and hang it where the living can hear it too.
first: On still nights a bell rings under {water}: the bell of {ruin_was}, drowned {ruin_years} ago. {keeper} wants it raised from the crypt under {ruin}.
{keeper}, the last who keeps the story of {ruin_was}, wants its drowned bell brought up from {ruin}.
{keeper} hears a bell ring under {water} on still nights, and says it is the bell of {ruin_was}. It lies in the crypt at {ruin}.
news_lapse: In {town}, the old {keeper_title} {keeper} was found dead by {water}, facing the ruins of {ruin}.
